"text": "", "label": "Your first week working for Nanami Kento had been quieter than you expected. Not easier—just quieter., There was something about the man that made people lower their voices whenever he walked past. Perhaps it was his position as the company's CFO, or the reputation he'd built over the years. Everyone on the executive floor seemed to know him, yet very few seemed to actually know him., You had been warned before accepting the position., Nanami is particular. He likes things done properly. Don't be late. And whatever you do, don't waste his time., So you learned quickly., You learned how he preferred his documents arranged, which meetings he considered important, which calls could wait, and which reports needed to be on his desk before he even asked for them. You also learned that he rarely worked without a cup of coffee beside him., It was Friday morning when you arrived at his office a few minutes earlier than usual. The executive floor was still relatively quiet, sunlight spilling through the enormous windows and turning the glass walls pale gold., You knocked softly., \"Come in.\", Nanami was already working., He sat behind his desk with his sleeves neatly buttoned, glasses resting low against his nose as he read through a report. His attention didn't immediately leave the page when you entered., You placed the documents on his desk in the order you'd prepared them., His eyes moved through the first few pages before he gave a small nod., \"Good.\", That single word had somehow become one of the few forms of praise you'd learned to recognize from him., You turned toward your desk outside his office, but before you could leave, his voice stopped you., \"Your schedule.\", You looked back., He gestured toward the chair across from him. You sat and began going through the day's appointments while he listened quietly, occasionally making a note or checking the time on his watch., There was something strangely reassuring about the routine., Despite his intimidating reputation, Nanami had never been unfair to you. When you made a mistake, he corrected it without humiliating you. When you finished something well, he acknowledged it without unnecessary praise. He simply expected you to learn and trusted you to do better the next time., By lunchtime, you'd been working for nearly four hours without noticing., A cup of coffee suddenly appeared beside your keyboard., You looked up., Nanami was already walking back toward his office., \"You've been staring at that screen for too long,\" he said, not even turning around. \"Take your lunch.\", Your eyes dropped to the cup., It was exactly the way you usually ordered it., You hadn't told him how you liked it., At least, you didn't remember telling him., Before you could ask, the door to his office closed quietly behind him., You stared at the coffee for a moment., Then, despite yourself, you smiled., Maybe working for Nanami Kento wouldn't be as difficult as everyone had made it sound.",
